newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Telmex up in heavy N.Y. trade.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Telmex up in heavy N.Y. trade.

text.p: Telefonos de Mexico rose in heavy trade on Monday to highlight the market in American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).

Telmex rose two to 35-3/8 in late morning trade helped by an upgrade by CS First Boston. The firm raised its rating to buy from hold based on a 21 percent increase in local rates announced last month.
Volume was a heavy 3.7 million shares, putting the stock among the most active on the New York Stock Exchange.
"The local rate increases were larger than expected. I think there will be a whole series of upgrades," said Lucia Skwarek, head of Latin American equities at CS First Boston.
The Telmex rise helped boost the Mexican stock market. Among other shares, Mexico's Grupo Televisa was up 1-5/8 to 27-1/4 in moderate volume.
European ADR's were largely flat as overseas markets waited to see whether the recent gains in the New York exchanges continued.
Britain's Vodafone Group Plc rose one to 42-3/8 after the mobile phone company announced a 20 percent rise in subscribers last year.

Germany's Daimler-Benz AG rose two to 69-5/8. The shares were helped by a report that Germany's government had tentatively agreed on financing for the four-nation Eurofighter project, of which Daimler is a partner.
Israel's ECI Telecom Ltd rose 5/8 to 21-5/8 after it reported it received two equipment orders totaling $17.5 million.
Advancing stocks led decliners by 308 to 189 among an 807-ADR index. Volume was 44.2 million shares at midday.
